messages:
sarah: heads-up: gpu-ephemeral CI started failing on quant-eval. Got socket timeout to node and then OOM within warmup. job: gpu-eval/branch-foo #456 — any quick triage steps? :eyes:

ci-bot: [CI] job gpu-eval/branch-foo #456 failed ~3m ago
- node: gpu-ephemeral-17
- failure: socket timeout to agent (10.0.3.45:2375), followed by process OOM-kill
- artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/456 (logs, dmesg, nvidia-smi)

miguel: requeue first. sometimes ephemeral nodes fail to pull sidecar and you get socket timeouts that cascade into OOM. can you paste pod logs? which image/tag? :thumbsup:

sarah: requeued: `cictl rerun 456 --node gpu-ephemeral-17` — rerun queued (keeping artifacts from failed run). image: redwood/runtime:quant-2026-03-16

cheng: quick checklist to run while rerun goes: 
1) confirm driver/runtime mismatch: `nvidia-smi` + `/proc/driver/nvidia/version`
2) grep dmesg for Xid: `dmesg | grep -i Xid`
3) agent logs for socket resets: `/var/log/agent.log` on node
4) check container memory/cgroup limits

sarah: pasting top of pod log from failed run:
```
Loading model shard 0...\nworker0: cuda init ok (CUDA 12.1)\nsidecar: connecting to agent 10.0.3.45:2375... socket timeout after 30s
worker1: trying to alloc 32768 MB GPU memory
OOM when allocating 32768 MB cudadev malloc
TRACE: cudaMalloc failed at src/alloc.c:452
```

olivia: if the image has runtime libs for 12.x but the node driver is older/newer you get weird hangs. run these on the pod/node:
```
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- nvidia-smi
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || true
```

miguel: also check node kernel for oops: `dmesg` may show `NVRM: Xid` and `GPU page fault` right before the killer. Xid 79 = GPU hang/watchdog often.

ci-bot: artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/456/nvidia-smi.txt, /artifacts/456/dmesg.txt, /artifacts/456/pod-logs.txt

sarah: attached nvidia-smi shows driver 535.54, CUDA runtime 12.1. nvcc not present in image (runtime-only). dmesg excerpt: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU hang` then `OOM killer invoked`

cheng: Xid 79 suggests a kernel driver hang/watchdog. Possible causes: long synchronous kernels, driver/kernel mismatch, or bad firmware. For quick mitigation try lowering concurrency/warmup and disable aggressive prefetching. Suggested env changes: `WARMUP_THREADS=2`, `BATCH_PREFETCH=0`. If that avoids the hang, we can schedule a canary driver rollback/upgrade.

sarah: doing a rerun with reduced warmup and prefetch: `cictl rerun 456 --env WARMUP_THREADS=2 --env BATCH_PREFETCH=0`

miguel: if rerun still flops, open infra ticket and request a targeted canary to revert to 535.50 (or try 535.60) on one node. cc @cheng

olivia: also collect `/var/log/kern.log` and `journalctl -u nvidia-*` from the node for the infra ticket. nudge infra to include the full kernel config if they rolled a patch recently.

sarah: rerun is running now. will report back in ~10m. thanks. :pray:

--- 8 minutes later ---

sarah: update: rerun finished — warmup reduction removed socket timeout (sidecar connected), but we still hit a soft OOM on shard 2 at step 42. attaching /artifacts/456/heap-trace.txt

cheng: soft OOM + prior Xid 79 still points to intermittent GPU hang or memory leak across shards. Steps: 1) run a minimal synthetic repro on gpu-ephemeral-17 (small busy-loop kernel) to see if it hangs; 2) if repro succeeds, bisect driver/kernel roll (create canary with previous driver); 3) if not reproducible, try increasing swap/cgroup limits to avoid soft OOM as temporary mitigation.

miguel: filed INFRA-789 driver rollout bisect, added logs and request to revert to 535.50 on canary. tagging infra on the ticket.

sarah: noted. I'll attempt the synthetic repro on that node now and dump kern.log if it hangs. will update INFRA-789 with outputs.

olivia: one more FYI — if you see frequent agent socket timeouts it sometimes indicates load on metadata service or node-sidecars starved. correlate with kubelet metrics.

sarah: thanks all. will follow up after synthetic run. /thread
